proposals.before: Zhu Shang was succeeded by Zhu Yan, who lost his title in Yongyuan 14 when his brother Zhu Bo was implicated in Empress Yin's witchcraft affair as her grandson by a daughter.
proposals.after: Zhu Shang was succeeded by Zhu Yan, who lost his title in Yongyuan 14 when his elder brother Zhu Bo was implicated in Empress Yin's witchcraft affair as her grandson by a daughter.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 兄伯 specifies that Bo was Zhu Yan's elder brother; the idiomatic rendering drops 'elder'.

proposals.before: He helped pacify Hebei, became magistrate of Yewang, and with Kou Xun of Henei held Luoyang at bay to the south and Tianjing Pass to the north until Zhu Xin and the rest dared not march out—merit that drew Guangwu east.
proposals.after: He helped pacify Hebei, became magistrate of Yewang, and with Kou Xun of Henei held Luoyang at bay to the south and Tianjing Pass to the north until Zhu Wei and the rest dared not march out—merit that drew Guangwu east.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 朱鮪 is read Zhu Wei (鮪 wěi); 'Zhu Xin' is a mistransliteration of the name.

proposals.before: He followed in pacifying Hebei, was appointed magistrate of Yewang, and together with Governor of Henei Kou Xun resisted Luoyang in the south and guarded Tianjing Pass in the north; Zhu Xin and others did not dare send out troops, and the Shizu came because of Liang's merit.
proposals.after: He followed in pacifying Hebei, was appointed magistrate of Yewang, and together with Governor of Henei Kou Xun resisted Luoyang in the south and guarded Tianjing Pass in the north; Zhu Wei and others did not dare send out troops, and the Shizu came because of Liang's merit.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 朱鮪 is read Zhu Wei (鮪 wěi); 'Zhu Xin' is a mistransliteration of the name.

proposals.before: In Yongchu 7 Empress Dowager Deng renewed the fief for Jing Bao's brother Jing Qu as marquis of Jianting.
proposals.after: In Yongchu 7 Empress Dowager Deng renewed the fief for Jing Bao's younger brother Jing Qu as marquis of Jianting.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 苞弟遽 specifies Qu was Bao's younger brother; the idiomatic rendering drops 'younger'.

proposals.before: Wang Jianshi was dragged down when his father Wang Yu and brother Wang Ping were found plotting with Prince Ying of Chu; he died on the public scaffold and the marquisate was abolished.
proposals.after: Wang Jianshi was dragged down when his father Wang Yu and younger brother Wang Ping were found plotting with Prince Ying of Chu; he died on the public scaffold and the marquisate was abolished.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 弟平 specifies Ping was Jianshi's younger brother; the idiomatic rendering drops 'younger'.

proposals.before: After the east was settled, Jianwu 7 ordered him north to open military colonies at Jinyang and Guangwu against the steppe raiders.
proposals.after: After the east was settled, an edict in Jianwu 7 ordered him north to open military colonies at Jinyang and Guangwu against the steppe raiders.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 七年，詔茂 means that in the seventh year an edict ordered Du Mao; the idiomatic rendering makes 'Jianwu 7' itself the subject that gave the order.

proposals.before: In Jianwu 9 he succeeded Lai Xi as middle general, joined Liu Shang in taking Hecheng, and completed the pacification of Wudu.
proposals.after: In Jianwu 9 he succeeded Lai Xi as middle general, joined Liu Shang in taking Hechi, and completed the pacification of Wudu.
proposals.reason: The Chinese place name is 河池, read Hechi; 'Hecheng' is a misreading of 池.

proposals.before: In the ninth year he replaced Lai Xi as middle general, led General Who Commands Wuwei Liu Shang and others in breaking Hecheng, and thereupon pacified Wudu.
proposals.after: In the ninth year he replaced Lai Xi as middle general, led General Who Commands Wuwei Liu Shang and others in breaking Hechi, and thereupon pacified Wudu.
proposals.reason: The Chinese place name is 河池, read Hechi; 'Hecheng' is a misreading of 池.

proposals.before: In Yanxi 2 Emperor Huan revived the line with Ma Cheng's descendant Ma Chang as marquis of Yiyangting.
proposals.after: In Yanxi 2 Emperor Huan revived the line with Ma Cheng's great-great-grandson Ma Chang as marquis of Yiyangting.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 成玄孫昌 specifies a great-great-grandson; 'descendant' loses the stated generation.

proposals.before: Learning that Liu Xiu was in Henei, he overtook him at Shequan, became a cavalry colonel, and with Feng Yi held the line against Zhu You and Li Yi—who murdered Liu Long's wife and children.
proposals.after: Learning that Liu Xiu was in Henei, he overtook him at Shequan, became a cavalry colonel, and with Feng Yi held the line against Zhu Wei and Li Yi—who murdered Liu Long's wife and children.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 朱鮪 is read Zhu Wei (鮪 wěi); 'Zhu You' confuses him with 朱祐 Zhu You, a different general.

proposals.before: Hearing the Shizu was in Henei, he at once caught up at Shequan and was made colonel of cavalry; together with Feng Yi he resisted Zhu You and Li Yi and others, and Yi thereupon killed Long's wife and children.
proposals.after: Hearing the Shizu was in Henei, he at once caught up at Shequan and was made colonel of cavalry; together with Feng Yi he resisted Zhu Wei and Li Yi and others, and Yi thereupon killed Long's wife and children.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 朱鮪 is read Zhu Wei (鮪 wěi); 'Zhu You' confuses him with 朱祐 Zhu You, a different general.

proposals.before: Twelve-year-old Liu Zhuang, the crown prince as Duke of Donghai, spoke from behind the curtain: "The clerk was only repeating what his superiors told him—about comparing land returns."
proposals.after: Twelve-year-old Liu Zhuang, then Duke of Donghai, spoke from behind the curtain: "The clerk was only repeating what his superiors told him—about comparing land returns."
proposals.reason: The Chinese 顯宗為東海公 says only that he was then Duke of Donghai; calling him crown prince is anachronistic at this point of the narrative.

proposals.before: Guangwu had a rapid-as-tiger general grill the clerk until he confessed exactly as the crown prince had said.
proposals.after: Guangwu had a rapid-as-tiger general grill the clerk until he confessed exactly as the young duke (the future Xianzong) had said.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 如顯宗對 refers to the Duke of Donghai; 'crown prince' is anachronistic here.

proposals.before: When Guangwu passed through Xiangcheng, Fu Jun, then a pavilion chief, brought the army in and was made a colonel—whereupon Wang Mang's men seized his mother, brothers, and entire clan and put them to death.
proposals.after: When Guangwu passed through Xiangcheng, Fu Jun, then a pavilion chief, brought the army in and was made a colonel—whereupon Wang Mang's men seized his mother, younger brothers, and entire clan and put them to death.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 母弟 specifies younger brothers (弟).

proposals.before: During the siege of Luoyang Zhu You's officer on the east wall secretly agreed to open the upper east gate for Jian Tan at dawn.
proposals.after: During the siege of Luoyang Zhu Wei's officer on the east wall secretly agreed to open the upper east gate for Jian Tan at dawn.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 朱鮪 is Zhu Wei (鮪 wěi), the Gengshi commander of Luoyang, not 朱祐 Zhu You.

proposals.before: Together with the generals he attacked Luoyang, and Zhu You's detached general who guarded the eastern city carried out a ruse, privately agreeing with Tan to open the upper east gate at dawn.
proposals.after: Together with the generals he attacked Luoyang, and Zhu Wei's detached general who guarded the eastern city carried out a ruse, privately agreeing with Tan to open the upper east gate at dawn.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 朱鮪 is Zhu Wei (鮪 wěi), not 朱祐 Zhu You.

proposals.before: At dawn Jian Tan rode in with Grand General Zhu You, who held for Emperor Guangwu, and together they fought the Luoyang commander Zhu You, who still served Wang Mang's regime, below the armory until mid-morning, when the Luoyang commander capitulated.
proposals.after: At dawn Jian Tan rode in with Grand General Zhu You and fought Zhu Wei below the armory, killing and wounding many, until breakfast time, when Zhu Wei capitulated.
proposals.reason: The Chinese distinguishes 朱祐 (Zhu You) from 鮪/朱鮪 (Zhu Wei); the idiomatic calls both 'Zhu You' and adds that the Luoyang commander served Wang Mang's regime, which is not in the Chinese (Zhu Wei was a Gengshi general).

proposals.before: Tan together with Grand General Who Establishes Righteousness Zhu You rode in at dawn and fought a great battle with Zhu You below the armory, killing and wounding very many; only at breakfast time did they stop, and the latter Zhu You thereupon submitted.
proposals.after: Tan together with Grand General Who Establishes Righteousness Zhu You rode in at dawn and fought a great battle with Zhu Wei below the armory, killing and wounding very many; only at breakfast time did they stop, and Zhu Wei thereupon submitted.
proposals.reason: 鮪 and 朱鮪 are Zhu Wei, distinct from 朱祐 Zhu You.

proposals.before: His son Ma Tan inherited but lost the fief when his brother Ma Boji was implicated with Yan Zhong in Prince Ying of Chu's plot.
proposals.after: His son Ma Tan inherited but lost the fief when his elder brother Ma Boji was implicated with Yan Zhong in Prince Ying of Chu's plot.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 兄伯濟 specifies an elder brother.

proposals.before: When true kingship faded into mere hegemony, houses like Qi still promoted Guan Zhong and Xi Peng in orderly succession, and Jin still ranked Xianchen and Zhao Shuai at Duke Wen's court—that was sharing power with merit wisely.
proposals.after: When true kingship faded into mere hegemony, houses like Qi still promoted Guan Zhong and Xi Peng in orderly succession, and Jin still ranked Xian Zhen and Zhao Shuai at Duke Wen's court—that was sharing power with merit wisely.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 先 refers to 先軫 Xian Zhen of Jin; 'Xianchen' is not his name.

proposals.before: Liu Liang once warned that Gaozu packed his government with old friends from Pei; Guo Ji mocked the Nanyang clique; Zheng Xing cautioned against letting generals run the ministries.
proposals.after: Zhang Liang, Marquis of Liu, once remarked that Gaozu relied wholly on old associates such as Xiao He and Cao Shen; Guo Ji mocked the Nanyang clique; Zheng Xing cautioned against letting generals run the ministries.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 留侯 is Zhang Liang, the Marquis of Liu, not a person named 'Liu Liang'; and 蕭、曹故人 names Xiao He and Cao Shen, whereas 'from Pei' is not in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Formerly Marquis Liu thought Gaozu wholly used Xiao and Cao old acquaintances, and Guo Ji also ridiculed that Nanyang had many illustrious; Zheng Xing again warned against meritorious ministers monopolizing office.
proposals.after: Formerly the Marquis of Liu (Zhang Liang) thought Gaozu wholly used Xiao and Cao old acquaintances, and Guo Ji also ridiculed that Nanyang had many illustrious; Zheng Xing again warned against meritorious ministers monopolizing office.
proposals.reason: 留侯 is the title Marquis of Liu (Zhang Liang); 'Marquis Liu' reads as a surname.
